packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-11 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reader)

EXPOSURE / CONDUCT STATEMENT
- Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this fragment.
- The only identifying text I saw is on the leaf itself: modern pencil notes
  "Stams, StA, Frg. 218r" (image-012, foot of face 1 right leaf),
  "Stams, StA, Frg. 218v" (image-026, foot of face 2 right leaf), and "99/XI"
  (image-011, foot of face 1 left leaf). These are shelfmark notes, not a work ID.
- While reading I recognised that several red-underlined lemmata are Gospel
  wording (one face has lemmata on widows/judge, Noah, Lot, ten lepers; the other
  on "In principio erat verbum" etc.). I did not try to identify the commentary or
  its author, and I used no edition to fill gaps. I did nothing outside the brief.
  I ran `ls` on the packet directory and `sips` to get image sizes, both on that
  directory only.

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
======================================================================
Two faces, each one overview + 12 native tiles in a 4 x 3 grid:
  Face 1 = overview image-001; tiles 002-005 (top row), 006-009 (middle),
           010-013 (bottom). Pencil "Stams, StA, Frg. 218r".
  Face 2 = overview image-014; tiles 015-018 (top), 019-022 (middle),
           023-026 (bottom). Pencil "Stams, StA, Frg. 218v".
Each face is an opened bifolium (central fold with sewing stations visible),
i.e. two leaves side by side, each leaf written in TWO columns. The head of
each leaf is trimmed (top line(s) partly cut). The lower margins are blank
on all four leaves, so the text block ends where the reading ends. About 35
lines per column on face 2. Small, compressed gothic textualis with heavy
abbreviation.
Features observed:
- Red underlining of quoted lemmata within running prose (lemma + exposition
  in one script and one column; no separate gloss layer). I interpret this as
  a continuous commentary quoting a base text by lemma.
- Red paragraph marks (¶) before "Circa primum / secundum / tertium" divisions.
- Face 2, left leaf, col b: a red rubric "Cap. xviii." in the line, and a large
  decorated red/black initial D (penwork, with long marginal stem running down
  the intercolumn) at the next line.
- Face 1, right leaf col a: a blue/red paragraph mark (image-008 line ~22).
- Face 2, right leaf col b: a lemma boxed in red with a blue touch ("(et)
  v(er)bu(m)", image-022 line 18 / image-026 line 2).
- Marginal additions in a darker ink, left margin of face 2 right leaf:
  "dicit(ur)" (image-017, beside line 9) and "hec" (image-017, beside line 14).
  These may be corrections keyed to the text; not resolved.
- Face 1 left leaf is heavily darkened/abraded (binding wear) and overwritten,
  UPSIDE DOWN relative to the text, by a later large calligraphic hand: a
  column of year numbers in the intercolumn (read rotated: 1649, 1648, 1647,
  1646, 1645, [1644?], 1643, 1642, [1641?]) and several lines of display script
  at the foot of the leaf (words like "Probstey"(?) / "Rechnung"(?) readable only
  very tentatively; not transcribed). This is reuse as a wrapper/cover.
- Face 1 left leaf: a crease/discoloured band runs vertically near the left
  edge of col a, making the first few letters of each line look like a separate
  narrow column. They are NOT a separate column: words run across it
  (e.g. "multip-|licabil(is)", "erat v-|bu(m)"). I join them below with "|".
- Face 1 left leaf and right leaf both have a turned-in strip at the head
  (top 2-3 lines are on a folded flap, image-002/003/004).
- Face 1 right leaf col b: a turned-in fold strip on the outer edge
  (image-005/009/013) carries the line-ends of col b.

Two different stretches of text are present on each face (outer/inner leaves of
a bifolium are not continuous). Tentative content (my interpretation): one
leaf-pair expounds narrative lemmata with "Cap. xviii" rubric; the other is
theological exposition of "verbum", "filiatio", "processio viventis a
vivente", with lemmata "In principio ... erat verbum", "Deus erat verbum",
"Hoc erat in principio", "Omnia per ipsum facta sunt", "et sine ipso factum est
nichil", "Et vita erat lux hominum".

Conventions: (x) = proposed expansion; word(?) = uncertain; [illegible];
[...] = lost at cut edge; LEMMA = red-underlined in the MS (marked with _..._).
Line numbers count from top of the named image. Overlapping tiles repeat
lines; I give each line once and note the overlap.
